Candidates for mayor to square off in Mississauga debate
items.summary: Poverty, housing and food security will be among the issues discussed when Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates meet on stage for the first major debate of the municipal election campaign in early October. Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network are co-hosting the mayoral debate on Oct. m. at FBM’s warehouse on Eastgate Parkway in the city’s east end. Organizers said the four top polling candidates — currently incumbent Carolyn Parrish, Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — will be invited to take part in the debate. Participants will be confirmed by Sept. 18. The debate is being held “to ensure that poverty alleviation, including income and housing security, and food security are key platform issues for Mississauga mayoral candidates,” event organizers said in an online description of the upcoming debate. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at right, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie will debate key Mississauga issues on Oct. 1. items.title: Stromedy Creator Kyle Godfrey Premieres Horror Short Simon Says at TIFF Lightbox
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga-based YouTuber Kyle Godfrey has released Simon Says, a 20-minute horror film centered on a remote cabin, a group of carefree twenty-somethings and an unsettling clown-like figure with unusual taste in party games. The outlet reports Godfrey, who has lived in both Mississauga and Milton, co-directs and stars in the film, building on earlier credits on Crated and The Mannequin Man. INsauga reports the film premiered at the TIFF Lightbox in Toronto last month, letting Godfrey move beyond the short-form videos he is best known for on his Stromedy YouTube channel. According to the outlet, Godfrey said he wanted to create stories with more depth and a real cinematic feel, contrasting the constant pressure of the next YouTube upload with the months spent building one story in filmmaking. INsauga reports Godfrey has built one of Canada's largest digital audiences over the years and has no plans to step back from YouTube despite the pivot into filmmaking. The outlet notes Simon Says is available to watch on YouTube and the streaming service Tubi.

items.title: Only Top Four Mayoral Candidates Will Take Part in Oct. 1 Mississauga Debate
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network will host a debate for the city's mayoral candidates on October 1 ahead of the October 26 municipal election. The outlet reports the event is organized to give candidates a chance to address income, housing security and food availability issues facing residents. According to a statement from the organizers, only the four candidates who are polling highest will be invited to take part, with the field confirmed by September 18. Mississauga.com reports the public can submit questions for the debate through an anonymous survey covering topics they want addressed, along with candidates' policy commitments and goals for their first year in office. The outlet reports that survey will also remain open until September 18. According to Mississauga.com, public registration for the debate itself opens in September, giving residents time to secure a spot before the event.

items.title: Cooksville Development Would Swap Two Houses for a Dozen Townhomes Near the QEW
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new development application submitted to the City of Mississauga proposes replacing two houses in Cooksville, north of the QEW, with 12 townhomes. The outlet reports the existing homes, along with any sheds or other structures on the properties, would be demolished to make way for the project, though the developer hopes to preserve mature trees along the rear and side lot lines. INsauga reports the townhomes would be split between two blocks flanking a common element condominium roadway, with access from Harborn Road. According to the outlet, five units are planned for the block on the west side of the private road and seven units for the block on the east side, with each townhome getting its own driveway and single-car garage. INsauga reports the driveways would have enough room to park an additional vehicle, and four visitor parking spaces, including one accessible space, are planned at the south end of the roadway.
